meta.title: Wing Fighter Strategy Guide
meta.tagline: Build stronger PvP formations. Understand your opponents. Invest where it counts.
meta.author: ashpool

content.html: Before attacking in PvP, look for a matchup you can actually win. Against a Dodge specialist, compare your Hit Rate with their Dodge. Against a Crit specialist, compare your Crit Resistance with their Crit Rate. If your counter is far behind, don’t force the attack: look for another target or consider a mirror matchup where your own Dodge or Crit is stronger. Pilots matter especially in those mirror fights, along with your drones, sentinel, and the rest of your build. This guide explains those choices, how to strengthen your formations, and how to spend resources wisely.

content.title: Three things to get right first

cells: Learn to read PvP matchups before attacking.

Check the opponent’s main strength and decide whether you have a credible counter. Hit Rate answers Dodge; Crit Resistance answers Crit. If the relevant stat falls far short, consider a different target before using an attack.
Improve Defense Break for the gear you use and both Physical Defense and Energy Defense. Good pilot stats help you beat opponents with more BP.
Build one dependable PvP formation before chasing every variation.
Get your core chips, drones, sentinel, and Mech Spirits working together. Develop a second formation to counter opponents your first build struggles against. Keep a PvE formation for boss rewards.

content.html: You have three saved formations. Most players keep one for PvE and use the other slots for PvP. Keep a PvP-ready setup in Formation 1 if you use Hyper Battlefield proxy mode: players have reported that proxy mode defaults to that slot.

content.title: Go straight to the part you need

cells: Look up the formulas or exact caps

content.html: Start with the opponent’s build, not your favorite formation. Against high Dodge, check whether your Hit Rate is close to or above it; against high Crit, check whether your Crit Resistance is close to or above it. If you cannot counter their main stat, you can sometimes win a mirror matchup: Dodge versus Dodge when your Dodge substantially exceeds their Hit Rate, or Crit versus Crit when your offense is stronger. Those fights depend heavily on the overall quality of your build, especially pilots, drones, and sentinel. If neither route gives you a real advantage, choose another target.

content.title: Check the opponent before choosing a build

content.html: First, identify the opponent’s main offensive or defensive strategy. Against Dodge, compare your Hit Rate with their Dodge; if your Hit is close to or above their Dodge, your Hit-focused formation is a strong option (often paired with Crit). Against a high-Crit opponent, compare your Crit Resistance with their Crit Rate; if your resistance is close to or above their Crit, favor your Crit-Resistance formation (often paired with Dodge). These are two different decisions. Against Burn, look for Burn Decrease and enough survivability. Also compare Defense Break and Defense, but do not choose solely by BP.

content.title: Choose chip stats that work together

cells: First choice against high Dodge when your Hit Rate is close to or above their Dodge. If your Hit falls far short, don’t assume Crit will carry the matchup.
First choice against high Crit when your Crit Resistance is close to or above their Crit Rate. If the resistance gap is too large, look for a different advantage.
A possible Dodge-versus-Dodge choice when your own Dodge is much higher than their Hit Rate. Compare pilots, drones, and sentinel strength before committing.
Can support a Crit-versus-Crit fight. If you cannot counter their Crit with resistance, consider whether your damage and overall build are stronger instead.
Let Burn do damage over time while limiting enemy crits in longer fights.

content.html: These stats do different jobs: Hit Rate counters Dodge; Crit Resistance counters Crit. Common chip pairings combine each counter with a second strength. But a counter only helps if you have enough of it. When you do not, mirror fights can work if your own specialty and supporting systems are stronger. Pilots are particularly important. It is also fine to skip a bad matchup instead of spending an attack hoping for the best.

content.title: PvP Crit / Hit: counter Dodge and hit hard

content.html: Use this formation against a Dodge-focused player when your Hit Rate is close to or higher than their Dodge. Hit is what answers Dodge; Crit is the damage stat commonly paired with it. If your Hit is nowhere near their Dodge, expect too many misses and consider another target. One alternative is Dodge versus Dodge, but only if your Dodge greatly exceeds their Hit Rate and you have the stronger supporting build, especially pilots, drones, and sentinel.

cells: SavagePlate brings fast direct damage. Stormquill instead weakens enemy Damage Boost. Choose based on whether you need more offense or protection.
Toad Lord can build Crit Damage from normal weapon crits and remove Burn stacks. Other useful swaps include Venom Scorpion, Flame Stinger, and Gloom Moon, depending on what the opponent brings.
Hit Rate when your opponent relies on Dodge and the extra Hit helps you reach or exceed their Dodge.
Use developed drones whose skills help the matchup. This is a core recommendation, not a fixed three-drone recipe.
Match PDB or EDB to your gear and PD or ED to the opponent’s damage type.

content.html: Example: if an opponent has high Dodge and your Hit Rate nearly matches it, Crit/Hit is a sensible attack. If your Hit Rate is far below their Dodge, switch plans rather than forcing the same formation. If your own Dodge is far above their Hit Rate, Dodge/Dodge may win through survival and stronger pilots, drones, and sentinel. Otherwise, save the attack for a more favorable target. The point is to find an advantage you can explain before fighting.

Do not pair Toad Lord with Evil Eye. Toad Lord needs your fighter and weapons to crit. Players report that Evil Eye redirects those crit opportunities into Burn Crit Rate, leaving Toad Lord unable to build its usual stacks. Keep Evil Eye in your PvE Burn/Crit setup, not this conventional PvP Crit setup.

content.title: PvP Dodge / Crit Resistance: counter Crit and survive

content.html: Use this formation against high-Crit opponents when your Crit Resistance is close to or above their Crit Rate. Crit Resistance is the counter to Crit; Dodge provides a separate way to avoid direct attacks, and healing can prolong the fight. If their Crit is much higher than your resistance, this may not be the right counter. You could consider Crit versus Crit instead, but only when your own damage and supporting build can win that exchange. If not, look for another target. Burn is a separate threat because applied Burn ticks cannot be dodged.

cells: Dodge + Crit Resistance. Choose it particularly when your Crit Resistance is close to or higher than an opponent’s Crit Rate. Dodge separately helps you avoid ordinary hits.
A developed Gridstar with gold Healing Enhancement is an accessible core. Arcglow and Doomblast offer different healing options as you progress.
Ladybug provides an emergency heal. Aqua Spirit and Berserk Dragon add lasting defense. Use the components you have while working toward this combination.

Sagittarius adds Burn damage during long fights; Apus is another accessible option. Fill the other drone positions with your best developed support rather than forcing an unfinished high-rarity drone.
Crit Resistance when you want to counter a Crit-focused opponent; choose Burn Decrease against Burn-heavy attackers.
A defensive pilot and fighter appropriate to the opposing damage type; Hardrock is one established option.

content.html: You do not need perfect endgame components to use a defensive formation, but the matchup still matters. First check whether your Crit Resistance can meaningfully offset enemy Crit. For a Dodge mirror, compare your Dodge with their Hit Rate: a large advantage can keep you alive while your pilots, drones, and sentinel decide the fight. Stronger pilots are often the difference between two players with similar chip strategies.

Ladybug heals a percentage of your maximum HP when you fall below its threshold. Healing Enhancement increases that heal, so a strong healing sentinel passive helps more than just the sentinel itself. Aqua Spirit also fits this strategy: its defensive bonus lasts for the rest of the battle, even if healing returns you to full HP.

Burn works well against high-Dodge players because Burn-drone skills do not use the normal Hit-versus-Dodge check, and Burn damage already applied keeps ticking. For this to work, your Burn Enhancement must overcome their Burn Decrease. You also need enough defense and healing to stay alive while the damage builds.

cells: Use three Burn drones if you equip Star Envoy. Two Ninjas and Sagittarius are a practical early trio; a developed Lich or Lyra can change the best combination later.
Arcglow or Doomblast supports longer fights. Glimshade can heal when the target is burning. Against powerful healing builds, consider Heal Reduction instead.
Star Envoy + Aqua Spirit + Ladybug is a defensive Burn combination.
Crit Resistance by default; matchup-specific counters as needed.
Match your Defense Break to your gear and your equipped pilot’s Defense to the threats you face.

content.html: This is a different strategy from PvE Burn/Crit. Your PvP Burn formation spends chip space on Burn Enhancement and Crit Resistance, then uses defensive Mech Spirits to survive. Evil Eye belongs to the PvE Crit-to-Burn conversion strategy we recommend, not this PvP formation.

content.title: PvE Burn: start with Burn chips, grow into Crit

content.html: For a boss-focused formation, first reach 100% effective Burn Enhancement. That is the maximum effective bonus against a boss with no Burn Decrease, not a special unlock. Early on, you will probably need Burn chips to get there. Over time, Camp Tech, native stats, and sentinel passives will provide more Burn Enhancement. Each time those sources improve, see whether you can replace a Burn chip with a Crit Rate chip without dropping below 100% effective Burn Enhancement. The long-term goal is maximum Burn Enhancement with all your chip slots helping Crit Rate.

cells: Use Burn chips to reach 100% Burn Enhancement. Replace them one at a time with Crit Rate chips when your non-chip Burn bonuses allow it.
Equip three Burn drones; two developed Ninjas are a practical start. Build a third drone such as Lich, Sagittarius, or Lyra over time.
Flashstrike provides a brief Damage Boost window. Use a developed alternative if it produces better boss results.
Evil Eye for Burn Crit conversion. Add Star Envoy (SSR) when available and equipped with three Burn drones. Use the third slot for damage or missing Burn Enhancement.
Equip a pilot whose Defense Break matches your gear: PDB for physical, EDB for energy. Continue improving that stat.

content.html: At maximum Evil Eye level, about 143% displayed Crit Rate converts into the 80% effective Burn Crit Rate cap against a target with no Crit Resistance. This is a useful PvE benchmark, not a target for every build or every opponent. Once both Burn Enhancement and Burn Crit Rate are at their caps, keep building your relevant Defense Break. The conversion table shows the numbers.

For example, a player with 90% native Burn Enhancement and a sentinel passive that adds 15% has 105% on paper, but only 100% is effective against a boss with no Burn Decrease. That player no longer needs a Burn chip and can use those slots for Crit Rate. This is how an advanced PvE Burn build can end up using only Crit chips.

content.title: What to change when a matchup goes badly

cells: If your Hit Rate is close to or higher than their Dodge, try Crit/Hit. If your Hit is far below their Dodge, consider a Dodge mirror only if your Dodge greatly exceeds their Hit Rate and your pilots/drones/sentinel are stronger. Otherwise skip the target or use a credible alternative.

If your Crit Resistance is close to or higher than their Crit Rate, try Dodge/Crit Resistance. If it falls far short, a Crit-versus-Crit attack is possible only when your own offensive power and supporting systems are stronger. Otherwise choose another target.

A mirror fight can work if your Dodge is far higher than their Hit Rate. Check pilots first, then drones and sentinel. Without that supporting advantage, both sides may survive without you gaining the upper hand.

If your Crit Resistance cannot counter their Crit, compare your own Crit offense and full build. You need stronger pilots, drones, sentinel, or another decisive advantage; matching their Crit build alone is not enough.
Switch to a Burn Decrease engine. Dodge does not remove Burn already applied.
Try a sentinel or passive with Heal Reduction so the opponent cannot recover as easily.
High Defense vs your Defense Break
Your attacks are being reduced by their Defense. Improve the Defense Break matching your gear, or choose a better matchup.
Your normal attacks miss or fail to crit

Diagnose the right stat separately: misses point to Hit Rate versus Dodge; hits that rarely crit point to Crit Rate versus Crit Resistance. For choosing a formation, start with which opponent strategy you can counter best.

content.title: How to use your three formations

content.html: Each of the three saved formations remembers your complete build: chips, equipment, pilot, drones, sentinel, and Mech Spirits. Switching slots restores them together. Keep options that answer the opponents you face most often, but remember that having three formations does not mean one must be a good attack against every opponent. Sometimes choosing a different target is the strongest move.

cells: Keep a PvP-capable build here if you use Hyper Battlefield proxy mode; players report it defaults to Formation 1.
Another PVP approach: for example, Dodge/Heal if slot 1 is Crit.
Often your dedicated PvE Burn formation. Advanced players may reuse a Crit formation for PvE and PvP, changing its drones and Mech Spirits for the mode.

content.html: Formation numbers do not dictate a particular playstyle. Keep different options ready so you can choose Hit against Dodge or Crit Resistance against Crit, depending on the opponent’s actual stats. If your PvE Crit build also serves as PvP Crit, remove PvE-only pieces such as Evil Eye before attacking another player. And after a boss fight, check what is equipped before defending in Planet Wars or Military Drills.

cells: The entire formation saved for defense when the event begins; locked for the whole event.
You can change your entire attacking build before each attack.
Whatever you have equipped at the moment they attack, even if it is your PVE build.

content.html: Easy mistake: you finish a boss activity in your PvE formation, then someone attacks you in Planet Wars or Military Drills before you switch back. Unlike Star Scramble defense, those modes use what you have equipped at that moment.

If you are not sure what to upgrade next, begin with pilots. Then look at the part of your main formation that is holding you back: chips that lack the right stats, unfinished drones, a weak sentinel passive, or Mech Spirits that do not support your strategy. The goal is a stronger working build, not progress in every system at once.

Battle Power (BP) is a measure of progression, but it does not tell you how effective those upgrades are in combat. A player with fewer but better-matched upgrades can beat someone with more BP. Keep improving pilots as your BP grows. A lean build can help in some matchups, but raw strength is valuable too, especially in Planet Wars and Military Drills.

Star Scramble is a team decision. Legions are matched in comparable roster sizes, so both average BP and total BP describe the strength of the roster. With the same number of players, lowering the average also lowers the total. Blackout deliberately values some lower-BP members: they handle item clears and fuel removal, helping higher-BP teammates eliminate opponents in a single attack. Their contribution is tactical, not just a lower matchmaking number. The exact matchmaking formula is not published, so treat BP as an important factor, not the entire rule.

In a Star Scramble attack plan, that often means assigning smaller members the preparatory work and preserving strong attackers for high-value clears. Lower BP only helps if those players are active and have a useful role.

Hyper Battlefield has five tiers, from BF5 (easiest) to BF1 (hardest). The jump from BF2 to BF1 is especially steep. Legion BP and previous results both appear to matter: adding strong players may move you up, and winning BF2 may also push you into BF1. The promotion formula is not published, so do not assume a fixed BP cutoff.

That is why leveling every sentinel past 80 or upgrading every piece of gear immediately is a choice, not an automatic priority. Some players pause gear around one-star rainbow to keep their BP efficient; others invest in extra raw strength for Planet Wars or Military Drills. Camp Tech and Mech passives can also increase BP. The better long-term habit is to keep your pilot investment moving ahead of BP inflation.

content.title: Pilots — The stats that keep you competitive

content.html: Pilots raise four combat stats: Physical Defense Break (PDB), Energy Defense Break (EDB), Physical Defense (PD), and Energy Defense (ED). The two Break stats help you deal more damage with matching gear. The two Defense stats help you survive attacks from other players. These affect far more than a single piece of equipment, which is why pilot development is such a good ongoing investment.

cells: Helps your physical-damage attacks overcome the opponent’s PD.
Develop this if you use physical gear.
Helps your energy-damage attacks overcome the opponent’s ED.
Develop this if you use energy gear.
Protects you against an opponent’s physical attacks and PDB.
Keep improving it, whatever gear you use.
Protects you against an opponent’s energy attacks and EDB.
Keep improving it, whatever gear you use.

items.html: Pilot gaps explain a lot of losses. If your PDB or EDB trails their matching Defense by a wide margin, your damage suffers. If your PD or ED trails their Defense Break, you take more damage. A clever chip setup can help, but it cannot always overcome a large disadvantage in these underlying stats.
Keep developing pilots alongside everything else. Well-built pilots make every formation more competitive. Even when equipment upgrades look exciting, do not let your pilot stats fall behind.

content.title: Equip the pilot for this matchup

content.html: You can equip one pilot at a time, and switching pilots is free. Every unlocked pilot still contributes Defense and Defense Break when unequipped, but the equipped pilot contributes about four times as much. The passive skill is shared either way; it does not get a four-times bonus. The one exception to free switching during play is your locked Star Scramble defensive formation.

For example, a six-star SR Lancelot contributes +80 EDB and +80 PD when unequipped. Put him in your equipped slot and those contributions become +320 each. After awakening, that rises to +100 unequipped or +400 equipped. That is why your first SR awakenings should focus on pilots you actually switch between.

Choose your first awakened SR pilot based on the damage type you deal and the damage type you most often face. A physical player who meets lots of energy opponents may awaken Hestia before Freya. If you use both physical and energy gear, developing all four combinations gives you more options. You can change pilots before each Star Scramble attack, but the pilot in your defensive formation is locked for the event.

There is no automatic “Freya first” or “Clotho first” rule. For a physical player, Freya helps when physical attacks are common, while Hestia or Brunhild helps against energy opponents. Your actual matchups decide which one you equip more often.

content.title: Build one Break type; defend against both

content.html: If you deal physical damage, build Physical Defense Break (PDB). If you deal energy damage, build Energy Defense Break (EDB). Every player should develop both Physical Defense (PD) and Energy Defense (ED), because the opponent decides which damage type you need to survive.

You only need to develop both Break stats as priorities if you regularly play both physical and energy builds. Do not spend scarce pilot resources trying to maximize an offensive stat your gear cannot use.

content.title: Pilot Evolution, Awakening, and Extra Shards

content.html: Unlock pilots as you acquire them. The first two evolutions cost Pilot Badges and provide substantial gains relatively cheaply; their Badge requirements are the same for N, R, SR, and SSR. Later evolutions need increasing quantities of that specific pilot’s shards. At higher stars, they can also require extra shards from other pilots. Many pilot shards arrive as random drops, though SR selectables are available in the Pilot Event, Hyper Battlefield shop, and other sources.

At six stars, a pilot is fully evolved but not yet awakened. Any shards you already have beyond the amount needed to reach six stars, as well as future drops for that pilot, become automatically usable as extra shards of its rarity. You do not need to exchange them manually. That creates a useful trade-off: finishing a nearly complete N or R pilot can give you more stats and unlock a pile of extra shards for later awakenings.

A good early target is to awaken two SR pilots you plan to equip for your main damage type, or four if you routinely switch between physical and energy gear. These are alternate pilots, not four simultaneous equipped pilots. Then work toward six stars on your N and R roster, both for their stats and for the extra shards future drops provide. After that, decide whether to awaken R pilots for accessible gains or additional SR pilots for stronger specific passives. SR awakenings cost much more, so the best choice depends on the passive you need and the resources you have. SSR awakening remains a long-term goal because the shards are difficult to acquire outside special events.

A useful way to choose the next six-star N or R pilot is to check three things together: how many shards it still needs, how much Defense or Defense Break it adds, and how many extra shards you will unlock immediately. Sometimes the stat gain matters most; sometimes the extra shards make the decision.

These are extra shards that can be used across pilots of the same rarity, not additional copies of the specific pilot being awakened. Awakening also costs Pilot Badges. In one supplied SR example, awakening required 1,800 Pilot Badges along with the shards shown above. Pilots continue contributing their Defense, Defense Break, and passive bonuses even when they are not equipped.

content.title: Train useful passives, not empty BP

content.html: Training Guides improve a pilot’s passive ability from level 1 through level 10. They also increase BP, but do not increase Defense or Defense Break. Each training level adds the same amount to the passive, while later levels cost more Training Guides. At a given level, the cost is the same for N, R, SR, and SSR pilots.

That makes spreading Training Guides across several useful passives a good starting strategy. SR and SSR pilots usually offer stronger PvP passives for the same guide cost, so raise a few of those to moderate levels before pushing one all the way to 10. Some N and R passives are mainly useful in PvE; training them adds BP without strengthening your PvP performance. But do train a passive that helps you win PvP fights, even if it raises BP.

Avoid old rules such as “you need X pilot points for every million BP.” Newer game systems have changed BP too much for those ratios to remain useful. Instead, compare yourself with actual opponents. Improve PDB for physical builds or EDB for energy builds, and keep both PD and ED moving forward. If you use both damage types, all four stats matter.

Think of pilots as something you keep improving, not a checklist you finish. If your attacks do little damage against similar-BP opponents, compare your Defense Break with their Defense. If you die too quickly, check their Break against your PD or ED. Those comparisons tell you more than a universal BP benchmark.

content.title: Chips — Build toward two useful stats

content.html: Your chip choices give a formation its identity. A Crit/Hit formation aims to land powerful weapon hits; Dodge/Crit Resistance emphasizes survival; Burn/Crit Resistance wins through lasting damage. For PvE, the progression is slightly different: use Burn chips to reach the maximum Burn Enhancement, then replace them with Crit Rate chips as other sources take over. The rest of your build should support the chips you choose.

content.title: Pick chips for the formation you actually use

content.html: The chip with the highest overall rating is not always the chip that helps your formation most. Check its actual stats. A Crit/Hit formation wants both Crit Rate and Hit Rate somewhere across its chips; a Dodge/Crit Resistance formation wants those two. In PvE, only replace a Burn chip with a Crit Rate chip if you can still maintain 100% effective Burn Enhancement for the boss you are fighting.

content.title: Use the Chip Factory without babysitting it

content.html: For normal daily use, turn on “Stop when chip rating increases.” The Chip Factory will pause when it finds a chip rated above the one currently in that slot. It saves time and is a sensible default, even though the rating does not always capture the best combination of attributes.

When you are changing builds, you may want to lower the minimum chip grade and look more closely at the results. A lower-rated chip with the right Burn or Crit stat can be a real improvement even if its overall score is worse. Set your target attributes to match the formation you are building. Use OR if either stat is useful; choose AND only if you require both attributes on the same chip.

The trade-off is your time. Leave the rating check on when you want easy daily production; screen more results manually when you are hunting a very specific stat combination. There is no single minimum grade setting that is right for everyone.

Burn is a reliable foundation for boss damage and helps in PvP against opponents who rely heavily on Dodge. Burning-drone skills and already-applied Burn damage do not depend on a normal Hit Rate roll, although drone normal attacks can miss. Choose three drones that work well together, then focus your upgrade resources on finishing them one at a time.

Start with one Ninja and work toward two well-developed Ninjas if you are using a Burn lineup. They are relatively accessible, and a finished lower-rarity drone can contribute more than a higher-rarity one that is barely developed. You can use them while gradually building a stronger third drone instead of waiting for three expensive SR drones.

cells: One or two developed Ninjas, plus your best available third Burn drone
Use what you already have; do not wait for the perfect three-drone lineup.
Lich’s Burn Damage bonus can help the trio while you save resources for later upgrades.
Two developed Ninjas + Sagittarius, Lyra, or another developed SR burner
A higher ceiling, but only invest heavily if you can keep progressing that drone.
Developed SR drones or a strong mixed R/SR trio
Pick by useful skills and completed upgrades, not rarity alone.

content.title: After Ninja, pick one drone to finish

content.html: Once your Ninja foundation is working, choose one next drone to develop rather than spreading scarce copies and materials across several unfinished projects. You can mix R and SR drones within the same formation; the question is which one you can realistically finish.

items.html: R drones: Usually more accessible to complete. Lich is appealing because its skill buffs Burn damage across all drones. Cerberus and Scorpion Lion have more situational interactions.

SR drones: More expensive to develop but potentially stronger once invested in. Sagittarius, Lyra, and Fornax are choices to consider. A developed SR can eventually replace a Ninja, but a half-finished SR should not automatically displace a strong drone you already own.

content.html: A developed R drone can still be valuable alongside SR drones when its skill supports the whole team. The mistake is not mixing rarities; it is spreading your resources so thin that none of the drones gets strong.

Burn stacks have a six-stack limit. A Burn-drone skill can add a stack, but adding a seventh does not create a seventh active stack: it replaces the oldest one. This matters when judging abilities that add extra stacks. Also remember that Burn-drone normal attacks can still miss, even though their skills and existing Burn damage do not use the normal Hit/Dodge check. The mechanics reference covers drone critical hits.

A drone has five passive slots, and full evolution develops each passive to level 7. That is 35 passive-level upgrades in total and requires 48 copies of that drone, including the original. Later star tiers consume multiple duplicates, so do not estimate the cost as one copy per upgrade. You can use drones of different rarities together.

When recasting drone passives, keep gold or purple results that actually support your build. A gold passive with the wrong effect is not automatically worth protecting. Recasting during Drone Events is especially useful because each Modified Chip spent counts as two toward the event’s spending milestone.

Transposition is a way to move good passive rolls to a better-developed drone. It costs 300 diamonds. Both drones must be the same rarity, have at least five stars, and have no unsaved recast results. The five passive types and colors switch places, but each drone keeps its own passive levels. For example, you can roll a great passive on a five-star donor, then transpose those passive types onto a much more evolved drone.
Lich: its level-4 skill gives +15% Burn Damage for all drones throughout the battle; the exact stacking relationship with other damage bonuses has not been independently verified.

Experimental Quick Reload deserves caution in Burn builds. The July mechanics research observed some situations where it increased the interval between Burn ticks from one second to as much as 1.5 seconds. That could reduce boss damage even if the passive sounds beneficial. Test it before committing to it.

content.title: Sentinels — Choose a job, then build passives

content.html: A well-developed N, G, or SR sentinel can be more useful than an unfinished SSR. Decide what the sentinel is supposed to do: heal you, deal damage, reduce enemy healing, or keep you alive while Burn builds up. Then develop passives that support that role.

cells: Arcglow for more sustain, or Doomblast as a longer-term SSR option
SavagePlate for repeated damage; Stormquill if you need to reduce enemy Damage Boost
Rendclaw when you need a stronger anti-heal answer
Flashstrike (N) for its short Damage Boost window
Compare against other developed sentinels using actual boss damage
Arcglow for sustain or Glimshade if enemies stay burned

content.html: You can keep more than one sentinel for different jobs. For example, a healing-focused sentinel may be your default defense, while an anti-heal sentinel can be the better choice against someone who relies on Ladybug and other recovery.

All five sentinel rarities (N, R, G, SR, and SSR) have four passive slots. Fully evolving one takes 40 total copies, including the first copy, and raises all four passives to level 10. Evolution also increases Attack and HP, but improving the passive bonuses is usually the biggest reason to pursue all 40 copies.

Sentinel level is separate from evolution. Overclock Chips raise the level and improve the active skill up to level 80. Levels 81–150 cost sharply more chips and raise raw stats and BP without making the skill stronger. Level 80 is a practical stopping point for many players, but pushing higher can make sense when raw strength is the goal. If you reset a sentinel, you can recover the Overclock Chips.

cells: Gold Healing Enhancement, then purple; Crit Damage Reduction or Sentinel Enhancement when useful.
Crit Damage, Crit Rate, Heal Reduction, and selected Sentinel Enhancement.
Crit Damage and useful damage buffs; Flashstrike can use a developed combination of multiple Crit Damage passives.
Healing Enhancement on Arcglow/Doomblast; Sentinel Enhancement if the sentinel’s own output matters.

content.html: At passive level 10, Healing Enhancement provides +100% for gold, +80% for purple, and +60% for blue. These bonuses add together. Gold Sentinel Enhancement adds +75% at level 10 and acts as a separate multiplier for eligible sentinel damage and healing. It does not multiply Ladybug or Cheat Death healing. Enemy Healing Reduction and Sentinel Reduction can offset the corresponding bonuses.

Not every heal uses the same bonuses. Ladybug and Cheat Death benefit from Healing Enhancement; Apus’s HP recovery does not. The mechanics research also indicates that Glimshade’s conditional heal benefits from Healing Enhancement but not from the Sentinel Enhancement multiplier. This is why “more Sentinel Enhancement” is not always the best answer for a healing build.

Start by looking for one gold passive that really helps the build. A second perfect gold can be expensive to chase. For more accessible sentinels, buying and merging another copy with a strong first roll may be better value than repeatedly spending resources to protect and recast passives.
This is also why the reverse-merge technique matters: it lets you transfer evolution progress onto a newer copy with a better passive roll.

content.title: The real cost of a sentinel recast

content.html: Every sentinel recast costs 20 Recast Cores, regardless of the number of locked passive slots. Locking slots protects good rolls, but each lock adds a separate Protection Core cost on every attempt:

Protection Cores are particularly expensive. At the first-pack rate of 15 for $3 (where available), locking one slot uses about $4 of Protection Cores per recast; two cost about $8; three about $20. Those amounts are in addition to the 20 Recast Cores. Later paid packs can be more expensive. Save the costly recasts for the sentinels where a better passive will make the most difference. The reference section models the odds of finding a specific gold passive.

content.title: Keep the better passive, not the older sentinel

content.html: Reverse merging lets you keep a great passive on a newer copy. Select the sentinel you keep, which has the passive you want, and the developed sentinel you sacrifice. The kept sentinel retains its existing passive rolls and receives the evolution stars. New passive slots gain new random rolls. All passive rolls on the sacrificed sentinel disappear.

For example, suppose you have an old 40-star Arcglow with mediocre passives and find a one-star Arcglow with gold Healing Enhancement. Keep the one-star copy and sacrifice the 40-star copy into it. You keep the gold passive and end up with a developed Arcglow. Level down the old sentinel before sacrificing it so you recover the Overclock Chips.

cells: 1,450% Attack every 4s; heals 30% of damage if enemy burning (PVP only)
Heals 360% Attack every 4s (PVP); +15% Final Damage Decrease for 2s
Heals 480% Attack every 4s (PVP); +10% Healing Enhancement each activation, up to +50%

content.html: Doomblast’s Healing Enhancement stacks build over time: each 10% stack begins <em>after</em) the heal that triggered it, so the next heal benefits. Flashstrike’s two-second Damage Boost can be helpful for damage dealt during that window, but the exact interaction with newly applied Burn stacks has not been independently tested.

content.title: Mech Spirits — Equip the three that fit

content.html: You can equip three Mech Spirits at a time. Their active skills should support your formation, but unequipped spirits still contribute collection stats and can help unlock named combination bonuses. Once you collect all spirits for a combination, activate that bonus in-game. Prioritize useful skills and combinations you can realistically reach instead of upgrading everything evenly.

items.html: Aqua Spirit (SSR): Its Emergency Shield grants +35% Final Damage Decrease the first time your HP crosses its threshold. At skill level 1 that threshold is below 30% HP; at level 13 it rises to below 96%. The protection lasts until the battle ends, even after you heal. That makes it especially valuable in healing builds.
Berserk Dragon (SR): Grants Final Damage Decrease from the start of the fight until the end: +10% at skill level 1, reaching +34% at level 13. Unlike Aqua Spirit, it has no low-HP trigger.

Ladybug (N): Heals the first time your HP falls below 30% in PvP. It restores 6.25% of maximum HP at skill level 1, growing to 21.25% at level 13. Healing Enhancement improves the result. Ladybug cannot be chosen with selectable Mech rewards, so Mech Event pulls are the main way to develop it.

content.html: For a healing formation, the synergy is straightforward: Aqua Spirit reduces damage after it triggers, Ladybug restores HP at low health, and Berserk Dragon adds protection from the start. Each is valuable alone, so build toward the combination instead of waiting for all three.

Aqua Spirit and Berserk Dragon contribute to the same Final Damage Decrease stat. Their listed +35% and +34% bonuses are valuable together, but do not interpret them as a literal 69% reduction in every incoming hit: the combat formula also depends on the attacker’s other damage modifiers.

items.html: Toad Lord (SR): Conventional weapon crits can trigger its effect every two seconds. Each trigger removes three Burn stacks from you and increases Crit Damage until the battle ends, up to eight stacks. At skill level 1, eight stacks total +60% Crit Damage; at level 13 they total +204%. It is less reliable against opponents with strong Crit Resistance. Do not pair it with Evil Eye, which Players report removes the normal weapon crit opportunities Toad Lord needs.
Venom Scorpion: Useful with conventional Crit offense when the opponent’s Crit Resistance does not prevent most of your crits. Against high resistance, expect less value.
Flame Stinger: A damage-finishing option when the opponent is low on HP. Gloom Moon is a Hit Rate counter for high Dodge; Battle Diva helps against heavy Crit.

Evil Eye (SR): Converts Crit Rate remaining after the target’s Crit Resistance into Burn Crit Rate. At skill level 1, every 10% eligible Crit Rate produces about 2% Burn Crit Rate; at level 13, it produces 5.6% and adds +25.5% Burn Damage Boost. It is a cornerstone of this PvE strategy, not a replacement for normal weapon Crit in PvP.

Star Envoy (SSR): Requires three equipped Burn drones. Every third Burn-drone skill has a chance to add a stack of Burn Damage Boost, up to five stacks. The activation chance increases as your Burn Enhancement exceeds the enemy’s Burn Decrease. The maximum stacked bonus is +125% at skill level 1 or +425% at level 13. This is a valuable long-term target, not something a new player must own to begin a Burn build.
Third slot: Use Dragon Emperor or another damage-focused spirit if available. Magic Armor can help while you are still short of 100% Burn Enhancement.

content.html: Mech Spirits improve their attribute bonuses during each four-level stretch. Every fifth level upgrades their main skill. The skill reaches level 13 when the spirit reaches level 60. You also get some benefits from spirits that are not equipped, so plan upgrades around the active skills and collection bonuses you can actually use.

content.title: Engines — Counter the damage you face

cells: You are attacking a high-Dodge opponent.
You are defending against Crit-heavy opponents; useful default for Star Scramble defense.
The opponent relies on that specific damage type.

content.html: Choose the engine that strengthens the counter you need: Hit Rate against Dodge, Crit Resistance against Crit, or Burn Decrease against Burn. Check the opponent’s actual stats before switching; a defensive engine is not automatically better just because you are defending, and an offensive engine is not automatically better just because you are attacking.

You can equip one engine at a time. Different engine grades can have equipped and shared bonuses, so check the values in your own game screen rather than assuming every engine offers the same multiplier.

content.title: Camp Tech — Buy the stat that helps

content.html: Camp Technology, Super Technology, and Legion Technology are separate upgrade systems. Camp’s Top Technology lets you improve matchup stats such as Crit Rate, Dodge, Hit Rate, Crit Resistance, and Burn Enhancement. Camp’s Super Technology includes Final Damage Increase and Final Damage Decrease, which affect damage more broadly. The best next upgrade depends on what your main formation needs.

For PvP, compare affordable Final Damage Increase, Final Damage Decrease, PvP Damage, and PvP Damage Reduction upgrades. For PvE Burn, more Burn Enhancement from Top Technology may let you remove a Burn chip and add Crit Rate. Before spending, ask whether the upgrade fixes a problem you are actually seeing in battles.

content.title: A practical order for Camp upgrades

content.html: These are priorities to compare, not a requirement to complete one category before touching another. Later levels can become very expensive, so a cheaper improvement in your second priority may be better than the next level in your first.

items.html: Final Damage Increase (FDI) and Final Damage Decrease (FDD): useful broad PvP improvements. FDI helps your outgoing damage; FDD helps reduce incoming damage. Prioritize whichever is affordable and addresses your current losses. The exact formula belongs in the mechanics reference, not in your first upgrade decision.
PvP Damage and PvP Damage Reduction: another set of broadly useful PvP bonuses. Compare the cost of the next level with FDI/FDD rather than assuming you must max one track first.
Burn Enhancement: especially valuable to a PvE Burn build until you can keep 100% effective Burn Enhancement without using Burn chips.

Hit Rate, Crit Resistance, Dodge, and Crit Rate: buy the stats that solve an actual problem in your matchups. Level 10 can be a convenient place to reassess costs, but it is not a required stopping point.

content.html: Basic Camp Technology upgrades Maingun, Winggun, Missile Attack, and HP across different camps. Some early levels may be quite cheap. Compare the price with the actual benefit to your fighter instead of following one fixed order for everyone.

Inside Camp → Super Technology, SkyEagle Tech provides FDI. Crystal Prism and Eternal Pivot provide FDD, and Source Essence provides another FDD path once unlocked. A Blackout recommendation has been to work toward level 80 on the first three and level 60 on other accessible lines. Treat that as one player’s plan; the right next level depends on what you have unlocked, current costs, and the opponents you face.

Titan sets are more than the stats printed on individual weapons. A complete matching five-piece set can increase the adjusted attack used by weapon damage and by drones, sentinels, and Mech Spirits. Make sure you are counting the actual equipped Titan pieces; owning or equipping a matching fighter alone does not give you a five-piece gear bonus.

items.html: Conqueror (physical): Use matching Conqueror Titan equipment with your Conqueror fighter to get the applicable set bonuses. The fighter and gear-set requirements are different things.
Destroyer (energy): A popular energy-damage direction. Titan Challenge seasons can favor different equipment, so compare your damage in the current season before spending scarce shards.
Thor (energy): Another energy set. It may be worth developing certain pieces for a Titan season, but evaluate them against the Destroyer pieces you already have.

content.html: The July mechanics model gives a 1.3× adjusted-attack factor for a complete five-piece Titan setup. Because several damage sources use adjusted attack, breaking the set may cost more damage than the new piece appears to add. This does not prove that every mixed setup is worse. Compare complete builds in the game mode you care about.

Before reclaiming or downgrading gear, check what it contributes to your active Titan set and how much upgrade material you will recover. Two pieces with similar-looking BP may offer different combat stats or effects. Do not assume every non-Titan piece is interchangeable.

If you do not have the matching Titan Winggun yet, Prism Winggun can be a useful temporary PvE choice. This comes from a Blackout player recommendation, not a tested rule that it is always the best interim option.

content.title: Legion Technology — Prioritize aerial PVP bonuses

content.html: Legion Technology is separate from Camp upgrades. It has three branches: Equipment Reinforce for weapon and armor stats, Damage Increase for damage bonuses against target types, and Enemy Weakened for reducing damage taken from those types. It uses Legion Points and Stars.

For PvP, pay attention to two upgrades that explicitly include other players: “Increase damage against aerial enemies (including players)” in Damage Increase, and “Reduce damage from aerial enemies (including players)” in Enemy Weakened. Their listed maximum level is 100. These can help across a wide range of PvP attacks and defenses, so they deserve sustained investment. That does not mean you must max both before improving your weapons.

Equipment Reinforce lets you improve individual weapons through Base Attack, Attack Rate, Crit Rate, and Crit Damage. Instead of following one universal ranking, start by looking at what damage your current weapons actually contribute:

items.html: Upgrade a weapon that matters to your damage. Compare Maingun, Winggun, and Missile performance in your current formation. The best choice may differ between Conqueror and Destroyer.

Choose the stat for the situation. Base Attack raises direct output. Crit Rate matters when your attacks can still gain from more crits, including against PvP Crit Resistance. Crit Damage helps most when you already land crits reliably.
Do not dismiss Attack Rate. More attacks can compete with bigger hits. Compare current cooldowns, damage, and upgrade prices; a single fixed order cannot capture every build.

content.html: For example, the mechanics model lists a rainbow Titan Winggun at roughly 1.6 seconds between shots with a damage coefficient of 0.09, and Missile at about four seconds with a coefficient of 0.225. Those numbers partly offset one another before considering weapon attack values, crits, and other bonuses. The point is not to memorize them; it is to compare what the weapon actually contributes before spending.

Keep Armor Base HP in mind too. If you are dying before your damage can matter, more survivability may help more than the next weapon upgrade. If PvP is your main focus, aerial-enemy bonuses usually deserve attention ahead of bonuses limited to bosses or ground/sea enemies. Check what you would lose in PvE before resetting any Legion Technology.

Most event milestones reset when a new event starts. Saving enough to reach a meaningful reward threshold is often better than spending every ticket or chip as soon as you get it. Use the table below to plan, then check the live event screen before committing: rewards and thresholds can change.

content.title: Know the milestone before you spend

content.html: Several events let you complete up to four reward rounds in one event. A full round gives the complete milestone rewards, but the best stopping point is not always the end of a round. The Mech Event is the clearest example: its early milestones can be valuable enough to justify stopping at 100 pulls.

cells: 100 pulls is an efficient partial target; 500 (400+100) can be better than stopping at 400, if affordable
Save enough for a full 300-pull round; diamond pulls can help reach another round
Bank for a complete round; purchase milestones reset each event
8,000 Rhenite eligible spend; up to 4 rounds
Use buy/sell refunds and event-credit drone recasts
No verified universal target in this guide

content.html: The Mech Event has 400 pulls per full reward round. Because the rewards in the first 100 pulls can be especially attractive, two practical stopping points are 100 pulls when resources are limited, or 500 pulls if you can afford to finish a 400-pull round and claim the first 100 pulls of the second. Do not assume 400 is always the best place to stop. Check the current reward screen before spending, as the exact rewards have not been independently verified for every event. Ladybug has no N-class selectable, so random Mech Event pulls are particularly important for developing it.

This does not mean you should spend 100 pulls in every Mech Event no matter what. Check how close you are to a larger target, what rewards are currently offered, and whether you are saving for another event.

content.title: Drone Event — How resale changes the cost

content.html: The Drone Event tracks 8,000 Rhenite of qualifying spend for each complete reward round. Up to four rounds are possible, and progress resets at the next event. When you buy a drone, its full price counts toward the milestone. If you sell it afterward, you get 80% of its purchase price back. That means 8,000 Rhenite spent entirely on drones costs only 1,600 Rhenite net after reselling them.

Shop refreshes cost 10 Rhenite each. They count toward event spend, but unlike drone purchases, cannot be resold or refunded. So a round that reaches exactly 8,000 total spend costs roughly 1,600 plus 80% of what you spent on refreshes. For example: 26 refreshes cost 260, plus drone purchases of 7,800, for 8,060 total event credit. Selling the drones returns 6,240, leaving 1,820 net Rhenite spent. The slight overshoot above 8,000 is included in that example.

Drone recasts are another way to contribute: each Modified Chip spent on recasting counts as two toward the Drone Event milestone. You do not get those chips back, so save useful recasts for event weeks rather than rerolling just to fill a meter. Your net Rhenite cost depends on purchases, refunds, refreshes, and recasts. The Drone Event Calculator can help plan a round. With a Volley Vortex pass, completing four rounds may be easier; some active players can complete two or three without one.

A full Pilot Event reward round takes 300 pulls, and up to four rounds may be completed in one event. Milestone progress resets between events. Save Recruitment Tickets until you can reach a full round rather than buying scattered partial rewards. Active players may manage one round, and sometimes two with diamonds. SR pilot selectables are especially useful for developing the pilots you plan to equip and awaken.

A full Sentinel Event reward round requires 8,000 Sentinel Chips spent. Progress resets at the next event, and up to four rounds (32,000 total spend) can be completed in one event. If you cannot reach 8,000, saving for the next event is often better than spending partway toward a milestone you will lose. Finishing a round awards a selectable SSR sentinel in addition to anything purchased from the shop.

The shop offers four free refreshes a day. Paid refreshes cost 10 Sentinel Chips each. Free and paid refreshes advance the SSR refresh counters, which carry over between events. One SSR is guaranteed after every 20 refreshes in that counter. A random bonus SSR can appear earlier without resetting the 20-refresh count.

There is also a separate preferred-SSR counter. Choose the SSR you want. After five nonpreferred SSR appearances, the next refresh guarantees your preferred SSR; you do not have to buy those five to advance the counter. Changing your preferred selection does not reset it. When the preferred SSR appears, the counter resets even if you do not buy that copy.

One useful tactic is to use the free refreshes before the event until your preferred SSR appears in the shop. Then stop refreshing. When the event starts, purchase that SSR so its 1,000-chip price counts toward the new 8,000-chip milestone. You can buy only one copy per SSR appearance. Depending on refreshes and luck, a full event round may produce roughly four or five preferred copies through the shop, plus the selectable SSR reward. Lower-rarity purchases can help finish the spending milestone, but watch your inventory space. Extra slots have cost 500 diamonds.

Fully evolving an SSR sentinel requires 40 total copies, so treat it as a long-term investment. Collecting the right sentinels for a combination can also provide a bonus. Activate that bonus manually once you have the required sentinels; its behavior after selling one of them has not been verified.

content.title: Daily diamonds — Spend on your current bottleneck

content.html: Before refreshing a daily challenge or buying shop resources, ask what you are trying to finish: a pilot awakening, a drone evolution, a sentinel passive, or an event round. That answer should determine your diamond spending.

One full daily spending routine has been roughly 540 diamonds: 140 on engine parts, 100 each on three daily challenge resources (300 total), and 100 on Chip Factory parts. This is an example of an aggressive routine, not a requirement or a target for every player. Check which supplies you are actually short of before buying any of them.

If your diamonds are limited, it is better to fund the upgrade that helps your current build most than to buy a little of everything. Leave room to save for the Pilot, Mech, Sentinel, or Drone Event milestone you are planning to complete.

This section keeps the exact numbers and less certain interactions in one place. Use it when you need to calculate a matchup, compare a particular passive, or check whether an assumed cap is real. You do not need to read it before making progress with the main guide.

content.title: Defense Break vs. Defense — Exact math

content.html: Defense Break is an offensive stat; Defense is the matching defensive stat. For physical damage, compare your PDB against the target’s PD. For energy damage, compare your EDB against the target’s ED. The difference between those values changes your outgoing damage. Reverse the comparison to understand incoming damage: their PDB versus your PD, or their EDB versus your ED.
If your Break ≥ enemy Defense (neutral or bonus zone):
Damage Multiplier = 1 + ((Your Break − Enemy Defense) / 1000)
If your Break < enemy Defense (penalty zone):
Damage Multiplier = 1 / (1 + ((Enemy Defense − Your Break) / 1000))

You only need the gap between Break and Defense to apply the formula. At equal values, the multiplier is 1.00×. A positive gap increases damage; a negative gap reduces it. For example, if your PDB is 300 above their PD, the bonus-side formula gives 1.30× before other modifiers. The reverse comparison tells you how well your defenses hold up against the opponent.

When your Break equals their Defense, damage is at the neutral 1.00× multiplier. The effect changes smoothly as the gap changes: parity is a convenient comparison point, not a sudden cliff. Increasing Defense Break above parity can still help, so do not stop just because the two numbers match.

Below parity, a given negative gap reduces damage by less than the same positive gap increases it. That is because the penalty uses a reciprocal formula. The table shows both directions so you can see the size of the difference:

cells: Closing a deficit improves every hit.
At −500, damage is about two-thirds of normal.

content.html: When your Break is far below the opponent’s Defense, closing that gap can be a very valuable upgrade. But the formula has no magic threshold: compare the cost of more Break with your other available improvements.

content.title: Stat caps and which attacks use them

content.html: Most of these are effective caps after accounting for the opponent’s defenses. A displayed stat above a cap may still help in PvP because the opponent cancels some of it. For example, 150% displayed Crit Rate against 70% Crit Resistance leaves 80% effective Crit Rate.

cells: Effective after opponent Burn Decrease. PVE bosses generally have none; PVP may require more than 100% raw to reach the cap.
Your dodge minus opponent's hit rate; raw dodge can exceed 80%.
Your crit rate minus opponent's crit resistance; raw crit can exceed 80%.
80% effective for ordinary direct crits and for Burn Crit Rate; displayed Crit Rate may exceed 80%, which matters for Evil Eye conversion.

content.html: Different attacks follow different rules. Normal weapon hits and drone normal attacks can miss against Dodge. Drone skills, sentinel skills, and Mech Spirit skills generally do not use that same Hit Rate roll. This is why a Burn-drone skill can still damage a high-Dodge opponent even if ordinary attacks miss.

items.html: Normal weapon and drone attacks: Hit Rate and Dodge matter. Weapon crit chance uses global and weapon-specific stats; drone normal attacks normally need Spot Weakness to crit.
Drone, sentinel, and Mech Spirit skills: generally hit without the normal Hit Rate check, and normally do not crit.
With Evil Eye: Burn-drone normal attacks and skills gain a special way to crit using converted Crit Rate.

content.html: This distinction explains why a sentinel that deals damage through a skill does not need Hit Rate in the same way your normal weapon attacks do. It also explains why improving Dodge cannot stop a Burn skill that has already applied its damage-over-time effect.

content.title: How much Burn Enhancement is useful?

content.label: Hard cap
content.html: The burning-drone enhancement multiplier is capped at 2.0× (a maximum +100% effective enhancement), and floored at 1.0×. In the combat-mechanics model, the net bonus depends on your Burning Enhancement minus the enemy’s Burning Decrease. That means how much raw enhancement you need depends on the actual target:

A quick example: against an opponent with 50% Burn Decrease, 100% raw Burn Enhancement leaves you with only 50% effective enhancement. Reaching the full 100% effective bonus would require 150% raw. This is why “100% Burn” is a natural PvE target but not always enough for PvP.

items.html: PVE against a boss with no Burning Decrease: 100% raw Burning Enhancement reaches the 100% effective bonus cap. Beyond that, more enhancement adds nothing against that target. Do not assume every PVE enemy has identical defenses without checking.
PVP vs. opponent with no Burn Decrease: Same as PVE, 100% raw = 100% effective. Past 100% does nothing.
PVP vs. opponent with 50% Burn Decrease: Need 150% raw burn to deliver 100% effective. Burn chips past 150% start to over-shoot.
PVP vs. opponent with 100% Burn Decrease: Need 200% raw burn to deliver 100% effective. Still capped at 100% effective, just takes more raw to get there.

content.html: The central rule is effective Burn Enhancement = your raw Burn Enhancement minus the target’s Burn Decrease, capped at +100% and floored at 0% for this damage multiplier. Against a boss with no Burn Decrease, 100% raw is enough. Against a PvP opponent with 50% Burn Decrease, you would need 150% raw to reach the same 100% effective bonus. The floor means Burn Decrease can remove this bonus but does not push this multiplier below its unenhanced 1.0× baseline.

Once your other bonuses supply enough Burn Enhancement against a PvE boss, change spare Burn chips into Crit Rate chips. That is the foundation of the advanced PvE Burn/Crit progression described earlier.

There are two separate numbers to keep in mind: displayed Crit Rate and effective critical-hit chance. Regular critical hits cannot exceed an 80% effective chance after subtracting the target’s Crit Resistance. Your displayed Crit Rate, however, can rise much higher. Evil Eye uses the eligible displayed Crit Rate, including the amount above 80%, to create Burn Crit Rate. Burn Crit Rate has its own 80% effective cap.

Evil Eye (SR Mech Spirit) converts Crit Rate left after the target’s Crit Resistance. At skill level 1, 10% eligible Crit Rate converts to about 2% Burn Crit Rate. At level 13 (Mech Spirit level 60), 10% converts to 5.6%, and Evil Eye also grants +25.5% Burn Damage Boost at battle start. If the PvE target has no Crit Resistance, approximately 142.9% displayed Crit Rate reaches the 80% Burn Crit Rate cap at maximum Evil Eye. Players generally observe little or no PvE Crit Resistance, but that assumption has not been independently verified for every enemy.

cells: Max Evil Eye Burn Crit Rate

content.html: For PvE Burn, the useful sequence is: first reach 100% effective Burn Enhancement; then build Crit Rate until Evil Eye can reach 80% effective Burn Crit Rate; then keep improving Defense Break for your chosen gear type. More Crit Rate beyond the PvE target may still help when you switch that formation to conventional PvP Crit and face high Crit Resistance. Remove Evil Eye for that PvP setup. Players report that its conversion leaves Toad Lord without the normal weapon crits required to trigger, so the two should not be recommended together.

Without Evil Eye, drone normal attacks do not use your ordinary global Crit Rate. They need the Spot Weakness passive to crit. Raging Assault increases the damage of those drone crits, so it is most useful when you already have a way to land them. Spot Weakness can work on its own; Raging Assault does little for a drone that cannot crit.

items.html: With Evil Eye: Burn-drone normal attacks and skills can crit using Evil Eye’s converted Crit Rate and the global Crit Damage multiplier. That replaces their normal Spot Weakness/Raging Assault crit calculation for these attacks.
Burn ticks: The separate damage-over-time ticks do not themselves crit. Burn Crit Rate refers to the eligible Burn-drone attacks, not every individual damage-over-time tick.

content.html: My current preference is Lich among accessible R Burn drones, because its skill helps Burn damage across your whole drone trio. Cerberus and Scorpion Lion depend more on specific conditions. The July mechanics research did not prove an exact damage ranking, and Lich’s interaction with Sagittarius or Star Envoy is still uncertain.

cells: Listed +15% burn-damage bonus; exact stacking with other burn buffs unverified
A broadly useful team bonus, but do not count it as an independent 1.15× multiplier on every Burn tick. It may share the same bonus pool as other Burn buffs.
255% skill coefficient and +3.5% listed bonus per Burn stack; exact interaction unverified
The bonus depends on current Burn stacks. Mechanics research suspects it multiplies the skill’s damage rather than simply adding to its listed coefficient, but the exact interaction needs testing.
+1 burn stack when recoil is active
More Burn stacks can help under the six-stack limit, but a new stack replaces the oldest when the target is already full. The recoil condition also has to be met.

content.html: If you cannot test every drone combination, favor a bonus that helps your full Burn setup reliably. Treat Lich as a practical recommendation, not a mathematically proven winner against the other R drones.

content.title: Sentinel recast odds and duplicate rules

content.html: Each developed sentinel can have up to four passive slots. The rates below describe what a given available slot might roll, not your chance of getting a perfect full set. Some passive combinations are restricted, so the exact odds after you lock several slots are not fully documented.
Gold rolls are uncommon but not impossibly rare. A specific gold passive, such as Gold Healing Enhancement, is much harder to find.

content.title: Cost of hunting a specific gold passive

content.html: This is a planning estimate, not a promise about the game’s actual random-number behavior. It assumes that every unlocked passive slot has an independent 0.5% chance to roll the one specific gold passive you want. Locking a good existing roll protects it but leaves fewer open slots for the next attempt.

The dollar estimates assume 20 Recast Cores per attempt at $3 for 20. They exclude the separate cost of Protection Cores, which can become much larger once you lock slots. They also ignore free materials. Duplicate-passive rules could affect the real probability. Treat the table as a way to understand why perfect recasts get expensive, not as a spending recommendation.

Different colors of the same passive can coexist: for example, Gold Healing Enhancement and Purple Healing Enhancement can occupy separate sentinel slots. You cannot rely on getting two copies of the same type and color. The exact handling when some rolls are unavailable is not fully documented, so treat the probabilities as estimates.

A sentinel with one great gold passive and several useful supporting passives is already a success. The odds of landing a second exact gold can be expensive, and those same materials might make your drones, pilots, or another sentinel stronger. Chase a second ideal gold when the rest of your build is ready for that investment.

Some Blackout battle logs suggest that when two sentinels fire at the same instant, the higher-BP player’s sentinel may activate first. This is not confirmed by controlled testing, so do not build a strategy that depends on that firing order.
